thesis: Howard Marks argues that to achieve above-average investment returns, one must depart from conventional behavior and place active bets, as consensus opinions are already baked into market prices. He explains that while active investing carries the risk of below-average returns if those bets are wrong, there is no way to win without taking such risks, making the ability to select correct strategies and execute better than others essential for distinguishing performance.
